protocol.application: Two separate CPU-2 windows, each PHP/baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline/PHP, fresh result cache each run, OS caches warm. No window pooling. Actual analysis timers; hardware counts cover the entire command. Five files and twenty findings, matching exit/stdout/stderr.
protocol.controls: All valid samples retained. First short controls, five seeded long pairs, then a separate five-pair confirmation for shared frames and relative self after their regressions. Five deep pairs per size and five mixed 100-million-iteration pairs. No window pooling.
protocol.memory: Memcheck with system heap routing; three minimal/deep reference-escape programs, exact PHP output, zero invalid-memory errors. Leak detection was not enabled.
protocol.limits: 6 GiB aggregate, zero swap, exclusive lock, all processes inherit boundary. Native x86-64 only; no new JIT lowering or ABI.

limitations: Correctness repair, not a speedup claim.

Relative-self return control regresses in both confirmation windows, by about 9.05 percent in the second. Main-executor normalized instruction sequence and size are identical, and instruction counts are unchanged; linked addresses shift by 64 bytes. This establishes no additional executed work but does not identify the exact hardware cause.
The integrating task accepts the isolated correctness repair because the baseline uses freed Rc storage and crashes. The regression remains a required control for subsequent performance changes.
Existing closure callable lifetime after echo is independently reproduced and remains unfixed; it is not a reference-array escape failure.
No ARM64 native performance evidence, whole-application allocation count or JIT change.
